identity.real_world_identity_notes: Manufacturer-derived heritage data specifies a five-speed Lamborghini manual and dry single-plate clutch. AMS2 accepts five forward gears and visibly models a five-speed dogleg H-pattern, resolving a conflicting secondary six-speed listing in favor of the manufacturer specification for this record.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a round rim without an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, the car stalled when moving from rest without physical clutch input.
Only five forward direct-gear bindings were accepted, and the cockpit showed a five-speed dogleg H-pattern.
There is no automatic throttle cut: clutchless upshifts were possible only after lifting and matching revs.
There is no automatic throttle blip: clutchless downshifts required a manual blip and rev match.
The simulator tests establish when clutchless shifts can be made, but do not establish whether historical authentic running shifts should use the clutch; those clutch fields remain unknown.

The identity is confirmed against the correct specification, which is the check the C3.R failed. Lamborghini's heritage sheet gives this car a 5,707 cm3 V12 of 540 CV and lists the later Diablo GTR separately at 5,992 cm3 and 590 CV, so the gearbox wording read here belongs to the SV-R rather than to a neighbouring model.

The dogleg gate is not evidence of a racing gearbox. The contemporary road Diablo SV is itself described as a gated dogleg five-speed, so the gate came with the car this one derives from and implies neither different internals nor dog engagement. The dataset already holds two dogleg synchromesh cars in the M3 Sport Evolution and the 190E Evo II, so the pairing is unremarkable.

The car was not homologated as a vehicle, as expected for a one-make series car. No FIA HistoricDB vehicle form exists for the SV-R, and ACI Sport's safety-cage register lists it with an explicit "/" in the form-number column. That register has no gearbox or technique columns, so no homologation route to the construction exists for this car and none should be sought again.

Clutch use on running shifts is unestablished and no reviewed source speaks to it. Lamborghini's sheet gives the clutch hardware - dry, single plate - which is what the clutch is and not when the driver uses it, and no Supertrofeo regulation or period technical source found states either. Both fields stay unknown.

The construction is established as synchromesh from the one source that characterises it, and it settles the downshift blip with it. The blip becomes optional as authentic technique, and the requirement the guided drive found is carried as an AMS2 override. That dissolves the contradiction the previous classification recorded: the record no longer asserts through the blip a construction its gearbox_type leaves open. It now deviates from the dogleg synchromesh archetype on its two clutch gaps alone, which are the only fields still open on this car.
Live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.
The car required clutch input from rest and accepted five direct-selected dogleg gears.
Clutchless shifts required manual rev matching: throttle lift on upshift and manual blip on downshift. No automatic cut or blip was observed.

overrides.condition: AMS2 rejects a clutchless downshift until the driver blips, where the real car's synchromesh leaves the blip optional.

confidence.basis: Directly observed in the guided drive with Auto Clutch disabled: clutchless downshifts required a manual blip, and no automatic blip was present to supply it.

Manufacturer-derived five-speed evidence agrees with all five accepted AMS2 gears and direct cockpit inspection of the dogleg gate. Start, cut, blip, and rev-match behavior were directly tested; authentic running-shift clutch use remains unknown.

claims.basis: Official release and manufacturer identity evidence agree with the exact live CarModel and ST96 class observation.

Manufacturer-derived five-speed specification agrees with the five accepted direct gears and visibly modeled dogleg gate. The guided drive observed the gate in the cockpit and reported an ordinary dogleg, with first down and to the left of the racing plane.
Direct current-game tests and cockpit inspection establish the asserted start, lift, manual-blip, automation, pattern, and rim behavior; unsupported historical running-clutch claims remain unknown.

A marque-specialist technical sheet for the 1996 SV-R states "Lamborghini five-speed + reverse manual all-synchromesh". The wording is explicit rather than a blank or a dash, and it describes this car: the identity is confirmed against the manufacturer sheet's 5,707 cm3 and 540 CV, which separate the SV-R from the 5,992 cm3 GTR. It sits at medium because it is one secondary source rather than a manufacturer or series-primary statement - Lamborghini's own sheet is silent on construction rather than negative - and because the car was never homologated as a vehicle, so no primary route to the field exists. Falsified by a Lamborghini, Supertrofeo or period technical source describing the SV-R gearbox as dog-engaged, or by a gearbox supplier's own documentation.

A synchromesh matches the shaft speeds itself, so the blip is authentic technique rather than a requirement to engage the gear. This follows from the established construction rather than being stated by a source, and cannot be more certain than the construction it comes from. What the simulator demands is recorded separately as an override.

driver_summary: Lamborghini five-speed with a dogleg gate - first is down and left, outside the racing plane, so second through fifth fall in one straight fore-and-aft line.
